name: Spontaneous Intracranial Hypotension

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: International Classification of Headache Disorders (ICHD-3) Criteria for Spontaneous Intracranial Hypotension

criteria.description: Headache that worsens within 15 minutes of standing and improves within 15 minutes of lying down
Low cerebrospinal fluid pressure (<60 mmH2O) measured by lumbar puncture
MRI evidence of CSF leak or characteristic brain sagging
Demonstration of CSF leak on myelography or radionuclide cisternography
Improvement of symptoms after epidural blood patch or conservative treatment

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Orthostatic headache plus either low CSF pressure or characteristic imaging findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical supported by imaging and CSF studies; invasive testing reserved for uncertain cases

pathognomonic.notes: Headache worsens upon standing and improves when lying down

common.symptomName: Diplopia due to Cranial Nerve VI Palsy
common.notes: Abducens nerve palsy causing double vision
searchTerms: double vision from sixth nerve palsy
cranial nerve VI causing double vision

laboratory: Low opening pressure on lumbar puncture (<60 mmH2O)
imaging: MRI brain showing diffuse pachymeningeal enhancement
Brain sagging with descent of cerebellar tonsils
CT or MR myelography demonstrating CSF leak site
other: Improvement of symptoms after epidural blood patch

distinguishingFeatures: History of recent lumbar puncture or spinal procedure
Symptoms typically resolve within days to weeks
No low CSF pressure or imaging abnormalities
No CSF leak or low opening pressure

redFlags: Neurological deficits such as cranial nerve palsies
Signs of subdural hematoma or brain herniation
references: Schievink WI. Spontaneous spinal cerebrospinal fluid leaks and intracranial hypotension. JAMA. 2006;295(19):2286-2296.
International Headache Society. The International Classification of Headache Disorders, 3rd edition (ICHD-3). Cephalalgia. 2018.
Kranz PG, Gray L, Malinzak MD, Amrhein TJ, Luetmer PH. Spontaneous Intracranial Hypotension: Imaging Findings and Clinical Features. AJNR Am J Neuroradiol. 2016;37(9):1673-1679.
